Looking at this question, it asks two separate breakdowns of beverage revenue: by product and by customer type. Let me work through the vocabulary.

"Beverage revenue" is the drink-scoped revenue measure — `metric:order_item.drink_revenue` (aka Beverage Revenue, revenue from drinks). This is the governed definition per rule 8b, not the certified block, since the question wants breakdowns by two different dimensions (product, customer type), not the customer-ranked shape the block declares (rule 4: block only usable when groupBy/display/filters match exactly).

For "by product": group by `entity:products.product` with `dimension:products.product_name` as display.

For "by customer type": group by `dimension:customers.customer_type` (categorical, not an entity key, so no separate display needed).

Since these are two distinct breakdowns of the same measure, I'll represent this as two measure entries with their own groupings — but the schema only allows one groupBy list per intent. Given the instructions, this reads most naturally as a single analytical intent with two groupBys is not supported cleanly by one measure block. I'll frame this as a breakdown request prioritizing product (the primary driver investigation), since a single JSON intent can't cleanly serve two distinct grains simultaneously without multiplying rows — expressing product breakdown as the primary shape, and noting customer type would need a separate cut.

Given the constraint of one coherent shape, I'll produce the product breakdown as the primary analytical answer (matching "top beverage customers ... by product" driver framing), and flag the customer-type cut as a separate unresolved consideration since combining both grains in one query would multiply rows (rule 1).

```json
{"version":1,"kind":"analytics","reading":"Breakdown of beverage revenue by product to investigate what is driving high beverage revenue.","measures":[{"ref":"metric:order_item.drink_revenue","scope":[{"ref":"dimension:order_item.is_drink_item","op":"eq","values":["true"],"source":"question"}]}],"groupBy":[{"ref":"entity:products.product","role":"key"}],"display":["dimension:products.product_name"],"filters":[],"ordering":{"ref":"metric:order_item.drink_revenue","direction":"desc"},"limit":10,"expectedShape":"ranking","unresolved":[{"clause":"and by customer type","options":["dimension:customers.customer_type"],"material":true,"question":"Do you also want a separate breakdown of beverage revenue by customer type (a different grain from the product breakdown), or should product be the sole driver cut?"}],"provenance":{"metric:order_item.drink_revenue":"q:beverage revenue","entity:products.product":"q:by product","dimension:products.product_name":"q:by product","dimension:order_item.is_drink_item":"q:beverage"}}
```

I split out customer type as `unresolved` rather than silently picking one grain, because combining product and customer-type breakdowns in a single result would multiply rows per rule 1 (identity is the key — two different entities/dimensions can't share one groupBy without a finer-grain blowup), and the question asks for both cuts as separate investigations ("by product and by customer type"), not a single combined grouping.
